subject.title: Design: run lifecycle reliability — bounded liveness, abort⇒release, crash resume, completion drive

question: Should maintainers adopt this issue as the canonical staged run-lifecycle reliability umbrella, and what sequencing/compatibility constraints should Track A-D implementation PRs follow?
rationale: Source evidence supports the problem class, but the solution chooses lifecycle ownership, liveness policy, persistence, and Codex-wrapper behavior across stable gateway surfaces that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Adopt Staged Umbrella
options.body: Approve the four invariants as the canonical direction and require small Track A-D PRs with explicit source, tests, and live proof before closing linked reports.

options.title: Approve Track A/B First
options.body: Treat abort-to-release and truthful liveness as the near-term scope while deferring crash-resume and completion-drive decisions to later design work.

options.title: Keep Reports Separate
options.body: Decline the umbrella as a canonical design packet and continue landing narrow fixes only against the existing production reports.

recommendation.title: Adopt Staged Umbrella
recommendation.body: Approve the four invariants as the canonical direction and require small Track A-D PRs with explicit source, tests, and live proof before closing linked reports.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and self-assigned the umbrella and own the current Track A/B implementation stack linked from the issue.
